subject: Post-call: Performance SLO qualification (p95/p99) - hosted vs current provider
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call: Performance SLO qualification (p95/p99) - hosted vs current provider

Hi Samir / Grace -

Thanks again for the call earlier - good discussion. Quick recap and agreed next steps on performance/SLO qualification so we stay aligned: 

Summary of current state (from the call):
- Primary model: in-house LLM (chat) used for end-user support flows.
- Current provider reported: approximate p95 end-to-end latency ~380ms, p99 ~1.1s (Samir, feel free to correct below).
- Typical sustained throughput: ~50-60 QPS during business hours; concurrency spikes to ~20-24 concurrent chat sessions.
- Streaming: yes, chat uses token streaming for progressive UI updates.

Redwood hosted targets and questions:
- Target qualification goals you mentioned: p95 <= 300ms, p99 <= 800ms (end-to-end). Confirm?
- We need to validate both cold and warm cache behavior, and streaming tail-latency (first-token vs last-token time).
- Throughput baseline we should validate: 60 QPS sustained for 30 minutes, with concurrency up to 24.

Immediate next steps (action items):
1) Samir: please share a small sample of telemetry (latency traces) and an example request payload / prompt template + typical token counts. If you can drop a short CSV of recent latencies that helps.
2) Redwood (Marissa / Aditya): we'll run a hosted baseline test (synthetic load) against our hosted API config that matches your token sizes and streaming behavior. We'll capture p95/p99 and first-token streaming latency.
3) Schedule PoC run: propose Tuesday 2026-12-15 10:00-11:30 PT. If that works, we'll ask for short-lived API key or a replay capture to run tests against.
4) Follow-up call to review results: Wed 2026-12-16 TBD.

Attachments: redwood-slo-matrix.xlsx (SLO matrix + test plan), p95-p99-demo-recording.mp4 (short clip of our streaming behavior).

Questions for you now:
- Confirm the p95/p99 values you see today (end-to-end).
- Any blackout windows or production traffic constraints for running synthetic tests?

Thanks - I'll loop Aditya in on the PoC scheduling and test plan.

Best,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance SLO qualification (p95/p99) - hosted vs current provider

Thanks Marissa - quick clarifications below.

- Confirming current observed numbers (end-to-end, production monitoring): p95 ~380ms, p99 ~1.1s. These include our app-layer latency (pre/post processing) and the provider response time.
- Sustained throughput: peak window is ~60 QPS (mostly short requests, median ~120 tokens).
- Concurrency: spikes up to 24 concurrent streaming sessions.
- Streaming: yes, we stream tokens to the client; first-token appears within ~80-120ms in many cases but overall completion varies.

I've attached a sample telemetry CSV (finlytics-latency-sample.csv) with a short export from last week's peak window - includes timestamps, full_request_ms, provider_response_ms.

We are fine with your proposed PoC window on Tue 12/15 10:00 PT. For the PoC we can provide a short-lived API key or a replay capture of the requests; will confirm which by EOD tomorrow.

Also: please make sure the PoC measures both first-token and final-token latencies so we can compare streaming behavior.

Samir
Director of Engineering
FinLytics
samir@finlytics.com

Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance SLO qualification (p95/p99) - hosted vs current provider

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the sample CSV, Samir - that helps a lot. Confirming the PoC window for Tue 12/15 10:00-11:30 PT.

Plan for PoC (high level):
- Redwood will run a controlled synthetic load that mirrors your average token counts and streaming pattern (we'll replay the prompt templates you share).
- We'll run three phases: cold-start ramp, warmed steady-state for 30m at ~60 QPS, and a spike test to 100 QPS for 2m to observe tail behavior and graceful degradation.
- Metrics captured: end-to-end p50/p95/p99, first-token latency distribution (streaming), throughput, error rate, and CPU/GPU utilization on the serving side.

What we need from you before Tue: 
- Sample prompt templates + median/95th token counts.
- Confirmation whether it's ok for us to use a short-lived API key against your staging endpoint, or whether you'd prefer we run against a replay capture.
- Any IP allowlist entries for 54.172.0.0/16 (example) - Aditya will provide our test IP ranges once we confirm.

I'll assign Aditya to own the benchmark run. Laura - can you please confirm availability of the dedicated hosted pool (we may request a reserved instance for this run) and the test IP ranges?

Next call: Wed 12/16 to review results - propose 11:00 AM PT. I'll send a calendar invite after we lock the PoC details.

Thanks,
Marissa
